title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
lead: Intrusive thoughts and repetitive actions that are hard to get rid of are a disorder in their own right; with adequate treatment there is significant improvement.

blocks.sub: Intrusive thoughts and actions that are performed to reduce anxiety

items.d: The most frequent form: hand washing and disinfection compulsions.
Locks, the stove and electrical appliances are checked again and again.
Related to orderliness: everything has to be exactly in place.
These thoughts are unwanted and cause distress.

items.t: The thoughts are your own, but unwanted
items.d: The person accepts that the obsessions are their own thoughts, but unwanted, irrational, or unacceptable. Insight varies from person to person.

p: Obsessions are repeated, persistent, unwanted thoughts, images or impulses. They create distress, and the person tries to suppress or neutralize them with other thoughts or actions.
Compulsions are repetitive behaviors (hand washing, checking, ordering) or mental acts (counting, praying) performed as a response to an obsession or according to rigid rules.
Usually both components are present. The compulsion is performed to reduce anxiety or prevent a feared outcome, but it is either unrealistic or excessive.
In DSM-5 (2013), OCD was moved out of the anxiety disorders into a distinct category, “Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders”; ICD-11 followed a parallel step.

blocks.h: When should you see a doctor?
blocks.sub: By the criteria a doctor uses
items: There are repeated, unwanted thoughts, images or impulses that cause distress, and you try to suppress or neutralize them with other thoughts or actions.
There are repetitive behaviors or mental acts that you perform as a response to an obsession or according to rigid rules.
This takes more than 1 hour per day or causes significant distress and disrupts life.
The doctor rules out the effect of a substance or a medical condition, and another mental disorder that explains the symptoms better.

blocks.sub: The basis is exposure and response prevention

items.d: A first-line method: the person is exposed to the feared object or situation and does not perform the compulsion; anxiety gradually decreases (habituation).
list: the standard course is 12–20 sessions, 1–2 times per week; a more intensive format (daily) is also effective
the effect is substantial — this has been shown in randomized trials
the cognitive component of CBT is added to ERP: re-evaluation of thoughts about obsession, “thought-action fusion”, hyper-responsibility

items.d: SSRIs at high dose are first-line.
list: a higher dose than for depression is required
the effect appears at 8–12 weeks — slower than in depression
clomipramine (TCA) — second-line, when SSRIs do not work; anticholinergic and cardiac side effects are possible
in refractory cases — adding a low-dose atypical antipsychotic (risperidone, aripiprazole)

items.d: Gives no advantage over ERP alone.
list: in a randomized trial, ERP and ERP+clomipramine did not differ, and both were superior to clomipramine alone (response: ERP 62–86%, combination 70–79%, clomipramine 42–48%, placebo 8–10%)
medication is added when ERP is unavailable or when there are comorbid conditions
reducing family accommodation is a crucial treatment component
deep brain stimulation (target — ventral capsule and ventral striatum)
ECT is ineffective; studies of the rapid effect of ketamine and esketamine are ongoing

items.d: The course is chronic, but with adequate treatment there is significant improvement.
list: treatment is long-term; at least 1–2 years after remission
lifelong in case of multiple relapses

blocks.sub: A single session or a monthly package — we choose the format together

items: Is OCD just a love of cleanliness and order?

No. Clinical OCD causes distress and functional impairment, and the thoughts are felt as unwanted and irrational (ego-dystonic). Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder is a distinct disorder in which the traits are felt as one’s own (ego-syntonic).
Can obsessions be stopped by willpower?
No. OCD is dysregulation of the CSTC circuit and is not voluntarily controlled; ERP and SSRIs act at the neurobiological level.
Will an ordinary antidepressant dose do?
In OCD, SSRIs require high doses: the dose used for depression often does not respond. The effect appears at 8–12 weeks.
Doesn’t ERP cause trauma by keeping a person in a feared situation?
ERP is structured, stepwise, and conducted with patient consent; the method demonstrates proven long-term efficacy.
Will it calm things if relatives allow the rituals to be performed?
No. Permission for compulsions (accommodation) strengthens OCD; reducing family accommodation is a crucial treatment component.
